|---|---|---|
| Long trend | `close_200_sma` | COIN is sitting right at this benchmark, so it is the key strategic line. |

I left out `boll` (redundant with the 20-day mean), `macds`/`macdh` (redundant with `macd`), and `vwma` (overlaps the other moving averages).

- **Broad range:** from the data, the lowest low was 139.11 on 2026-07-31 (also 139.18 on 2026-06-26). The highest high was 222.35 on 2026-05-14 and the latest swing high was 208.33 on 2026-09-21.

- **October retracement:** from 201.07 on 9/22, price slid to 168.45 on 10/19. It has bounced to 177.08 on 10/21, which opened at 175.00 and closed in the upper part of a 172.04–180.60 range. Volume was 6.69M, so the bounce has no volume confirmation.
- **Choppy action:** closes alternate widely day to day, e.g. 172.89 (10/14), 183.81 (10/15), 173.16 (10/16). Single-day moves of about 6% show up in recent sessions.

## 4. Trend analysis (moving averages)
- **200 SMA (181.32):** falling steadily, from 188.91 on 9/21 to 181.32. Price is about 4.24 below it (close 177.08), so the long-term benchmark is not reclaimed.
- **50 SMA (178.94):** rising, from 167.50 on 9/21 to 178.94. Price is about 1.86 below it.
- **50/200 convergence:** the gap (200 SMA minus 50 SMA) has narrowed from about 21.4 on 9/21 to 4.69 on 10/16 and 2.38 on 10/21. A 50-over-200 crossover (golden cross) is mathematically near.
  - **Rising 50 SMA:** the 50 SMA window currently starts 8/12. The next sessions drop the 8/12–8/18 closes (149.04, 153.90, 148.47, 150.55, 146.23), which are well below current prices. If COIN stays near 177, the 50 SMA should keep rising by roughly 0.5 per day.
  - **Falling 200 SMA:** it has been falling about 0.3–0.4 per day recently. I cannot see the values it will drop, so this part is an assumption.
  - **Timing:** if both trends persist, a crossover could come within days. This is a scenario, not a forecast.
  - **Caveat:** this would be a lagging, mechanical signal. The 50 SMA is rising only because low August prices are rolling out of its window, while price itself is below both averages.
- **10 EMA (176.57):** it fell from 191.38 (9/28) to 176.46 (10/20) and ticked up to 176.57. The 10/21 close of 177.08 is just above it. This is the first close above the 10 EMA after three closes below it (10/16, 10/19, 10/20), but price had crossed it back and forth in the week before.
- **Pivot behavior:** since 10/7, closes have switched sides of the 50 SMA many times. For example, 179.39 was above on 10/9, 172.89 below on 10/14, and 183.81 above on 10/15. That points to a contested area rather than a clean trend.

## 5. Momentum (MACD and RSI)
- **MACD:** it peaked at 7.42 on 9/24, crossed below zero between 10/13 (0.20) and 10/14 (-0.62), hit a recent low of -2.38 on 10/20, and now reads -2.23. It is below its signal (-0.70) and the histogram is -1.53. Momentum is still negative, though the 10/20 low and slight uptick suggest the slide is slowing. There is no bullish crossover yet.
- **RSI (48.40):** neutral. It ran from 60.45 (9/22) down to 42.61 (10/19) and has recovered to 48.40. It has not reached oversold (30) or overbought (70) in the 30-day window shown. The lowest reading was 42.61, so there is no oversold exhaustion signal and no divergence I can verify from this data.

## 6. Volatility (Bollinger and ATR)
- **Bands:** 165.37 (lower) to 199.34 (upper), a width of about 34, narrower than about 37 on 9/21. The middle band is 182.35. Price sits below the middle at roughly 34% of the way from lower to upper band.
- **Band tests:** the intraday low on 10/20 (165.90) was just above that day's lower band (165.23), and the 10/15 low (165.80) was near that day's band (169.99 was the lower band, so it pierced it intraday and recovered to 183.81 by the close). These are observations of price touching the band, not proof that it holds as support.
- **ATR (10.84):** about 6.1% of the 177.08 close. It has eased from 12.68 on 9/21 but remains high.
  - **Stop distances:** 1.5× ATR is about 16.3 and 2× ATR is about 21.7.
  - **Sizing:** an ATR-based stop on COIN is wide, so position size has to be small to keep risk the same.

## 7. Levels to watch
These are reference points computed from the tool outputs, not validated support or resistance.
- **Overhead cluster (178.94–182.35):** the 50 SMA (178.94), 200 SMA (181.32), and Bollinger middle (182.35) sit within about 3.4 of each other. Above them are the 10/15 high (185.49) and the upper band (199.34).

- **Upside extreme:** the 9/21 swing high of 208.33.

- **Bias:** neutral to mildly cautious in the short term, inside a wide range.
- **Bullish evidence:**
  - the 50 SMA is rising;
  - a 50/200 golden cross appears near;
  - RSI has bounced from 42.61;
  - price just closed above the 10 EMA;
  - ATR and band width are easing.

  - MACD is negative and under its signal;
  - the 10/21 bounce came on lower volume (6.69M);

  - closes are whipsawing around the averages.
- **Scenarios:**
  - **Constructive case:** a close above the 178.94–182.35 cluster with MACD turning back up would support a move toward the 185.49 high, and the golden cross would then carry more weight.

- **Risk:** because of the whipsaw and a 10.84 ATR, treat single-day signals (a close above the 10 EMA, for example) as low-confidence until they are confirmed over several sessions.
